objective: Re-run the CBFS field inversion with the regularization preconditioned by the baseline adjoint sensitivity, so that a unit of penalty costs the same everywhere in the domain rather than being cheapest exactly where the objective is most responsive, and measure whether the geography gate moves
rationale: The inversion's regularization is an unweighted pull of the correction toward unity with a hand set weight, applied identically in every cell. Under that choice the optimizer buys objective reduction most cheaply where the sensitivity is largest, so the correction concentrates by construction wherever the adjoint is loud, independently of where the model is actually wrong. The geography gate has now failed twice under that formulation, at 29.0 percent before the objective repair and 26.9 percent after, against a bar of more than 50 percent, while a loss audit of the same domain found the declared window carrying 41.2 percent of the loss on 8.4 percent of the cells. The correction and the loss are in different places, and the standard cure for that shape in inverse problems is to whiten the prior by the sensitivity rather than to move the window or relax the bar. This item buys the experiment. It is deliberately filed as a successor to the zero compute diagnosis rather than beside it, because if that diagnosis returns a low correlation between correction magnitude and baseline sensitivity there is nothing to whiten and this purchase should not be made. Filing it now, priced against measured evaluation cost rather than against an analogy, is what lets that decision be taken on evidence in one step instead of two
gate: Pre-registration frozen before the first evaluation, on the pattern the F7a re-gate specification establishes, declaring the whitening operator, the weight calibration, the evaluation budget and every threshold. G-W1, CONTROL, must run first and must reproduce: the baseline correction at the archived final iterate must reproduce the published G1 value of 0.25847 and the published G2 value of 26.9 percent from the archived arrays. If it does not, STOP and report -- the comparison has no origin. G-W2, the whitened arm: G2 measured identically to the published definition, same 2,100-cell top decile, same declared window, same cell-centre test. PASS if G2 exceeds 50 percent. FAIL if it does not. G-W3, the objective must not be bought back: G1 in the whitened arm must remain at or below 0.70, the original bar. A whitened arm that crosses G2 by abandoning the objective is a FAIL of the whole item, not a partial pass, and this is declared here so it cannot be renegotiated afterward. G-W4, ungated and reported: the difference field between the whitened and unwhitened corrections, and the fraction of the top decile that changes membership. IDENTITY TEST, per Verification Charter 2a. Q1, what makes this FAIL: G2 staying below 50 percent under whitening, which would mean the geography is not a regularization artefact. Q2, could a wrong treatment still pass? YES, and by a route worth naming: whitening by the sensitivity mechanically pushes correction away from high-sensitivity cells, so if the high-sensitivity cells happen to sit outside the window, G2 rises for a reason that has nothing to do with turbulence. That is why G-W3 gates the objective at the same time -- a correction that moved into the window without keeping the objective reduction has not found the model error, it has found the null space. And it is why the preceding zero-compute diagnosis is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: it measures where the high-sensitivity cells are, so this arm's outcome can be read. EXTERNAL REFERENT, per Verification Charter 6a: NONE for the gate itself. G2 is measured against a window this lab declared, using this lab's own solver and mesh, and no published value exists for the fraction of a correction field lying in a window. Stated rather than implied. The window's PHYSICAL anchoring does have one, the Bentaleb, Lardeau and Leschziner large eddy simulation of this configuration distributed on the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource, and the pre-registration must state the separation and reattachment locations it brackets.
cost_basis: Priced against measured evaluation cost on this exact case, this exact design variable set and this exact tolerance, not by analogy. The immediately preceding reinversion billed 320.13 core minutes for 16 evaluations, an average of 20.0 core minutes per evaluation, and the separately measured anchor evaluation at the same primal tolerance took 599 seconds of wall at two cores, which is 19.97 core minutes, agreeing with the average to three parts in a thousand. The final state cold control plus write out was measured twice on this line, at 8.10 and 8.54 core minutes. So 16 evaluations at 20.0 plus one control at 8.5 gives 328.5, taken here at 340 to carry the contended case, where the same evaluations measured 26.5 to 27.1 core minutes under contention. Basis gross, on the charter's binding unit of wall seconds times ranks divided by sixty. An independent cross check from the earlier inversion at four ranks and a looser primal tolerance measured seventeen consecutive evaluations at 15.83 to 17.70 core minutes, summing to 335.98 over the whole item, so the per evaluation figure is stable across two runs, two rank counts and two tolerances. This is the best measured basis in the lab and it is stated with its known failure mode: the lab's forecasts score zero of three within twenty percent, and the one rotating case that overran did so by a factor of eight against an estimate built by analogy. This estimate is built by measurement of the identical operation and its residual risk is contention, not physics
expected_knowledge_gain: This is the first experiment in this lab that would separate a regularization choice from a physical claim in a field inversion, and both outcomes are publishable in the ordinary sense that a domain reader would recognise the work. A PASS says the correction concentrates in the separated region once the penalty is made geometrically fair, which converts the twice-failed geography gate into a statement about how field inversion must be regularized rather than about where model error lives, and it makes the reconstructed correction a defensible input to the learning stage that currently sits blocked behind it. A FAIL says the upstream concentration survives a fair penalty, which is the stronger physical result: model form error in this closure would then be set upstream of the region carrying the loss, and a closure correction learned only inside the bubble would be learning the wrong thing. Either way this line stops carrying an undiagnosed FAIL, which is its present state and has been for three days
hard_criterion_note: Extends the CBFS inversion family already on the record, on the same mesh, the same 21,000 design variables and the same solver build. The hardness floor was answered when that family entered and no new case is started

launch_prompt: S1 whitened reinversion. BLOCKED: do not launch until the zero-compute geography diagnosis (proposal s1-does-the-correction-land-where-the-error-is-or-where-the-sensitivity-is) has returned a verdict. If that verdict is PHYSICAL, this item is REFUSED, not run -- report that and stop, because there is no sensitivity concentration to whiten. If SENSITIVITY-DRIVEN or UNDECIDED, proceed. Step 1, zero compute: write and commit the pre-registration, declaring the whitening operator explicitly (the per-cell prior weight as a stated function of the archived baseline gradient magnitude, with its floor and its normalisation both written down and justified BEFORE any evaluation), the evaluation budget, and all four gates verbatim from this proposal. Freeze it. Step 2: run G-W1, the reproduction control, from archived arrays at zero solver compute. If it does not reproduce, STOP. Step 3: the whitened arm, warm-started per the pre-registration, 16 evaluations HARD, 340 core-min HARD. setsid, launch_solve.sh registered, collector armed. Step 4: the final-state cold control and write-out. Step 5: grade all four gates and report. DO NOT amend the pre-registration after the first evaluation -- Verification Charter 2b makes amendment legal only while there is no answer to tune to, and after evaluation one there is. DO NOT move the window, relax the 50 percent bar, or redefine the top decile; those are the three degrees of freedom that would make this result unfalsifiable, and they are frozen. Record: evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/ or the ladder-b directory beside its siblings, measured_core_min written into this proposal so the calibration scorecard gains a fourth pair, and an honest verdict either way.
